history.dynasty: Not documented in available sources; Tevaram-era (early medieval)
history.summary: Shiva temple at Thiruvarur East Street (near the chariot base of the grand Tyagarajar Temple), Tiruvarur. One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the Tevaram hymns (Tirugnanasambandar; listed as the 89th Tevara stalam in Chola Nadu south of the Kaveri). Historical place name: Arurparavaiyunmandazhi. Legends: Shiva swallowed the mighty deluge sent by Varuna; Durvasa muni worshipped here; saint Sundarar recovered his eyesight in this temple's tank, and an eye symbol is visible on the Shiva lingam during abhishek. Devotees pray here for restoration of eyesight. CSV town Tiruvarur is correct.

name: Thoovanayanar Thoovainathar Temple (Tiruvarur)
town_description: Tiruvarur is an ancient temple town in Tiruvarur district, Tamil Nadu, best known for the vast Tyagarajar Temple complex (a Sapta Vidanga sthalam) and its deep roots in Tevaram Shaivism. It lies in the Cauvery delta region between Thanjavur and Mayiladuturai.
